Subject: Newton private deploy — initial throughput requirements

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking this on. Newton is moving forward with a VPC/private deployment and we need alignment on the sizing/throughput targets so procurement can lock the hosting window. High level:

- Expected steady-state: ~600 requests/sec for chat endpoints (avg 120 tokens per request), with 95th percentile latency target <= 220ms for streaming responses.
- Burst profile: sustained spikes up to 2.4k requests/sec for windows of 5-15 minutes during product launches (we expect 3-4 of these per month).
- Model mix: 60% llama-3-70b-ct, 30% instruction-tuned smaller models, 10% reranking/embeddings.
- Data residency: EU (Frankfurt) for a subset of customers, global otherwise — will need routing policy.

Can your team propose committed pool sizing (GPU counts, warm pool strategy, and recommended headroom) and the networking/readout constraints we should include in the SOW? I can share the spike telemetry if you want more granularity.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Newton VPC — draft capacity model and baseline proposal

Hi team,

I ran a quick sizing exercise based on the numbers Alex sent. Draft conclusions (details in attached spreadsheet — newton_vpc_capacity_model.xlsx):

- Baseline committed pool: 8 H100-equivalent GPUs provisioned with an optimized serving profile (mixed precision quantization on llama-3-70b-ct). This supports ~650 steady req/s at 95% latency <= 220ms assuming a batching window of 8-12ms and average 120 tokens/request.
- Recommended headroom: reserve a warm pool equal to ~50% of committed capacity (4 GPUs) to absorb typical spikes with <30s spin-up when paired with pre-warmed runtime snapshots.
- Burst runway: to safely cover 2.4k req/s spikes, plan for planned burst capacity (burst-tier instances) that can add an additional ~10 H100-equivalent GPUs for 15-minute windows. If Newton wants guaranteed <220ms during peak, we recommend increasing committed pool to 12 GPUs and reducing burst dependency.
- Networking: estimate egress peak at ~250 Mbps per GPU for model shards during peak token emission; cross-AZ replication should be avoided for low-latency paths — prefer single-AZ with multi-AZ failover and warm hot-standby.

Open items: model-level tokens/sec distribution, premium customer routing requirements, and whether Newton wants cost-first or latency-first posture for SLA contract.

Proposed next steps: 1) 30m sync to validate token profile and routing; 2) finalize SOW language re: warm pool spin-up times and invoiced burst minutes; 3) procurement timeline to attach to MPO.

Thanks,
Laura

Laura Bennett

Quick ops/architecture notes — tagging here so SOW and SRE runbooks line up: 

- Serving topology: prefer dedicated pod allocation per GPU with explicit KV cache affinity to avoid cross-node KV sync during hot prefixes. Multiplexing strategies (small-model routing + prefix caching) can reduce effective GPU QPS by ~18-22% in our simulations.
- Network considerations: if FRA VPC has a managed NAT egress with 100Gbps pipe, the per-GPU egress estimate from Laura seems conservative — confirm uplink oversubscription policy with Newton infra. We should include an egress policing clause in the SOW (throttle triggers, graceful degraded outputs).
- Autoscale behavior: warm pool should support fast allocation using pre-cached images and in-memory KV warmers; add a 3-step rollout for canary (10% traffic), staged ramp (50%), then full (100%) — document fallback to hosted model variants if provisioning fails.

Also attached a quick diagram showing traffic paths and egress zones (ml_inference_network_diagram.png).

-Jonas

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Newton MPO & next steps — committed sizing decision and procurement items

Alex / team — solid thread, thank you. Summary and asks so procurement can proceed: 

Summary decisions agreed (draft):
- Committed pool: 12 H100-equivalent GPUs in FRA (primary) + 4 warm GPUs reserved; this gives steady-state coverage and reduces reliance on short-term bursts for SLA-backed premium traffic.
- Burst policy: allow up to +10 GPUs for 15-minute windows billed as burst minutes; require 10-minute notice for scheduled launches (we can relax for emergency traffic but may have higher overage rates).
- SLA posture: premium customers get latency-backed SLA (95th <220ms) with agreed fallbacks — other customers best-effort.
- Network clause: egress policing and graceful degradation rules included; Redwood to run a 48-hour soak test during onboarding to validate egress assumptions.

Action items:
1) Priya — please attach the updated SOW language and send MPO to Newton for signatures.
2) Laura — update the spreadsheet to reflect 12-4 committed/warm split and add a cost delta for 12 vs 8 committed.
3) Jonas — prepare the runbook for warm pool spin-up and fallback routing to hosted models.
4) Alex/Kyle (Newton) — confirm whether multi-AZ cold-standby is required for compliance; if yes, we need to redo network egress math.

I've attached the MPO template (docsign_mpo.pdf stub) and will queue a procurement slot once we have confirmation. Planning note: if Newton wants guaranteed full-latency SLA during the 2.4k req/s bursts without increased pricing, we recommend an alternative: replicate to a second FRA carveout for active-active (higher cost).

I'll follow up with a short call invite for tomorrow to finalize SOW text.

Best,
Markus
